title: Scientists may have misread a 2-billion-year-old clue about Earth
hook: Scientists may have misread a 2-billion-year-old clue about Earth

beats.caption: Scientists may have misread a 2-billion-year-old clue about Earth
Imagine finding a diary and mistaking it for a history textbook.
beats.detail: We read the Earth like a document.
beats.narration: Imagine finding a diary and mistaking it for a history textbook. Sometimes science does the exact same thing.

beats.caption: Scientists found a chemical signature dating back two billion years.
beats.detail: A clue from deep in the past.
beats.narration: Scientists found a chemical signature in the rocks dating back two billion years.

beats.caption: We thought it proved a massive shift in the carbon cycle.
beats.detail: Global change was the assumed cause.
beats.narration: They thought it proved a massive shift in the global carbon cycle.

beats.caption: But new research challenges that entire interpretation.
beats.detail: It might be a local event.
beats.narration: But new research challenges that entire interpretation, suggesting the signal is not global at all.

beats.caption: It was likely a local event rather than a worldwide change.
beats.narration: It was likely a local event, created by magma, hydrocarbons, and hungry microbes.
